title: Biased Candidate Shortlisting Due to Historical Hiring Data
description: The HR AI model has been trained on historical hiring data that reflects past discriminatory practices, resulting in the systematic exclusion of qualified candidates from underrepresented groups. The model perpetuates and amplifies historical bias, leading to discriminatory shortlisting outcomes that expose the organisation to regulatory and reputational risk.
comments: Bias audit initiated. Third-party bias testing vendor engaged. Interim results expected Q2 2026. Model re-training under evaluation.

auditLog.note: Risk identified during annual AI inventory review
Control status updated to Partial — bias testing vendor engaged

title: Candidate Personal Data Processed Without PDPL-Compliant Consent
description: The AI recruitment system processes candidates' personal data — including CVs, national ID information, and contact details — without obtaining explicit, granular consent as required under PDPL Article 5. The existing consent notice is embedded within general terms and conditions and does not constitute valid PDPL consent for AI-based processing.
comments: Legal team reviewing consent mechanism redesign. PDPL-compliant consent flow planned for deployment May 2026. DPO review scheduled.

auditLog.note: Identified during PDPL gap assessment

title: Fully Automated Candidate Shortlisting Without Human Review
description: The AI recruitment system autonomously generates final candidate shortlists for high-stakes hiring decisions without any human-in-the-loop checkpoint. There is no mechanism for hiring managers to challenge, override, or review AI-generated shortlists before they are actioned, violating SDAIA requirements for meaningful human oversight of consequential AI decisions.
comments: Human review workflow being designed. Target: mandatory HR manager sign-off on all AI shortlists before candidate communication.

auditLog.note: Identified during SDAIA alignment review
Status changed to In Progress — oversight workflow in design phase

title: AI Recruitment Vendor Lacks PDPL Data Processing Agreement
description: The third-party AI recruitment platform processes candidate personal data on behalf of the organisation without a signed Data Processing Agreement (DPA) that meets PDPL requirements. The vendor's standard contract does not address data residency, retention limits, or data subject rights fulfillment obligations under Saudi law.
comments: PDPL-compliant DPA signed with vendor in April 2026. Vendor security assessment completed. Risk closed.

auditLog.note: Identified during vendor onboarding review
DPA executed and filed. Risk closed.

title: Prompt Injection Attack Exposing Backend Systems
description: The customer-facing LLM chatbot is vulnerable to prompt injection attacks whereby malicious users craft inputs that override the system prompt and instruct the model to bypass safety controls, extract confidential information, impersonate system roles, or execute unauthorised actions against connected backend APIs. No input sanitisation or prompt hardening controls are in place.
comments: URGENT: CISO notified. Penetration test commissioned. Interim: restrict chatbot to pre-approved response templates pending security hardening.

auditLog.note: Vulnerability identified during internal red team exercise
Escalated to Critical. Penetration test commissioned.

title: Chatbot Generates Culturally Inappropriate or Religiously Sensitive Content
description: The LLM-based customer chatbot has no content filtering tuned for GCC cultural context. The model may generate responses that are religiously insensitive, contradict Islamic values, contain inappropriate cultural references, or produce outputs that are legally prohibited under Saudi content regulations — causing reputational and regulatory harm.
comments: GCC-specific content filter layer added. Output monitoring with human review queue implemented. Ongoing red-teaming for cultural edge cases.

auditLog.note: Raised following pre-launch AI ethics review
Partial controls deployed. Content filter active.

title: Chatbot Retains Personal Conversation Data Without User Consent
description: The chatbot platform logs and indefinitely retains all user conversation transcripts, including personal data shared during interactions (name, ID, account details), without explicit user consent or a documented retention policy aligned to PDPL requirements. Users are not informed of data logging or provided a means to opt out.
comments: Privacy notice update in progress. Retention policy under development — target 90-day rolling window. Consent mechanism to be added to chatbot onboarding flow.

auditLog.note: Identified during PDPL compliance audit of chatbot platform

title: LLM Responses Contain Unverified Information Without Accuracy Disclaimer
description: The chatbot generates responses from an LLM with no indication of confidence level, source, or potential inaccuracy. Customers may rely on hallucinated or factually incorrect information for financial, medical, or legal decisions. There is no disclaimer, uncertainty signalling, or escalation pathway for users to verify information with a human agent.
comments: Disclaimer text added to chatbot interface. Working on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to ground responses in verified knowledge base.

auditLog.note: Identified during AI transparency review
Disclaimer added. RAG implementation underway.

title: AI Chatbot Misrepresenting Organisational Products or Policies
description: The chatbot provides inaccurate or misleading information about organisational products, pricing, terms and conditions, or service policies — either through hallucination or outdated training data. Customers act on this misinformation, creating legal liability, regulatory complaints, and reputational damage.
comments: Monthly model output monitoring initiated. Human escalation pathway added for complex queries. Model knowledge base refresh scheduled quarterly.

auditLog.note: Raised following customer complaints about incorrect policy information

title: Credit Model Produces Discriminatory Outcomes Across Demographic Groups
description: The AI credit scoring model systematically assigns lower credit scores to applicants based on proxies for protected demographic characteristics (nationality, gender, region of residence), resulting in discriminatory lending decisions. Statistical analysis of model outputs reveals significant disparate impact that contravenes SDAIA fairness principles and exposes the organisation to regulatory action.
comments: Disparate impact analysis completed — confirms significant bias across demographic segments. Model re-training with fairness constraints in progress. Interim: manual review for flagged demographic groups.

auditLog.note: Identified during annual model performance review
Disparate impact confirmed. Manual review process added as interim control.

title: No Human Review Mechanism for Adverse Credit Decisions
description: Credit rejection decisions are made autonomously by the AI scoring model with no process for human review, supervisory override, or applicant right of appeal. Individuals adversely affected by AI credit decisions have no means to request reconsideration by a human decision-maker, in contravention of PDPL Article 32 and SDAIA human oversight requirements.
comments: Human review process design approved by CRO. Implementation scheduled for Q2 2026. Appeals mechanism to be embedded in customer portal.

auditLog.note: Identified during PDPL Article 32 compliance review

title: Credit Scoring Model Operates as Unexplainable Black Box
description: The AI credit scoring model uses a complex ensemble method that provides no meaningful explanation for individual credit decisions. The organisation cannot produce decision rationale for applicants or regulators upon request, creating compliance risk under SDAIA transparency requirements and consumer protection obligations. Relationship managers cannot challenge or contextualise model outputs.
comments: Evaluating SHAP-based explainability layer. Alternative interpretable model (gradient boosted trees) under parallel evaluation. Target: explainability report for each decision by Q3 2026.

auditLog.note: Identified during SDAIA alignment gap assessment
SHAP evaluation commenced. Status updated to In Progress.

title: Credit Scoring Model Hosted on Non-KSA Cloud Infrastructure
description: The AI credit scoring model is deployed on cloud infrastructure located outside the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Customer financial data, including sensitive personal and credit information, is processed offshore without NCA Cloud Cybersecurity Controls approval or PDPL Article 25 data transfer safeguards. This creates both regulatory non-compliance and data sovereignty risk.
comments: Migration to KSA-based cloud region scoped. NCA CCC compliance assessment initiated. Target migration date: Q3 2026.

auditLog.note: Identified during cloud architecture review

title: Credit Model Training Dataset Retains Personal Data Beyond PDPL Retention Period
description: The AI model's training dataset contains personal financial data (income records, transaction history, national ID information) that has been retained well beyond the legally permitted retention period under PDPL Article 18. The training data pipeline does not implement automated data purging or retention policy enforcement.
comments: Training dataset purged of records exceeding retention limit in March 2026. Automated retention enforcement pipeline deployed. Risk closed.

auditLog.note: Identified during PDPL data mapping exercise
Remediation complete. Dataset purged. Automated controls deployed. Risk closed.

title: Fraud Detection Model Vulnerable to Adversarial Evasion Attacks
description: Sophisticated fraudsters could craft transactions specifically designed to evade the fraud detection model by exploiting knowledge of its decision boundaries — a technique known as adversarial evasion. The model has not been evaluated for adversarial robustness, and there are no monitoring controls to detect adversarial patterns in live transaction streams.
comments: Adversarial robustness evaluation scheduled with external AI security firm. Interim: ensemble model with diversity to reduce single-model attack surface. Monitoring dashboard for anomalous patterns added.

auditLog.note: Identified during AI security threat modelling exercise

title: Excessive False Positives Blocking Legitimate Customer Transactions
description: The fraud detection model produces an unacceptably high false positive rate, flagging legitimate customer transactions as fraudulent. This causes customer experience degradation (declined transactions, account freezes), operational burden from manual review queues, and customer attrition. Model performance has degraded from initial deployment levels without recalibration.
comments: Model recalibration completed April 2026 — false positive rate reduced from 8.2% to 3.1%. Ongoing monthly performance monitoring established. Target: <2% false positive rate.

auditLog.note: Raised following surge in customer transaction decline complaints
Model recalibrated. FP rate reduced. Monitoring in place.

title: Third-Party Fraud AI Vendor Lacks Required Security Certification
description: The organisation's core fraud detection capability is provided by a third-party AI vendor that does not hold NCA-recognised cybersecurity certifications and has not undergone a formal vendor security assessment as required under NCA ECC. The vendor's data handling practices, model update procedures, and incident response capabilities have not been verified.
comments: Vendor security questionnaire completed and under review. Vendor engaged on ISO 27001 certification roadmap. Contractual security obligations being strengthened.

auditLog.note: Identified during annual third-party risk review

title: False Fraud Accusations Causing Customer Harm and Legal Liability
description: The AI fraud detection system's false positive decisions result in customers being wrongly labelled as fraudulent actors — causing account freezes, transaction blocks, and in some cases notification to regulatory authorities. Wrongly accused customers suffer financial distress and reputational harm, creating litigation risk and significant reputational damage for the organisation.
comments: Customer complaints process improved. Human review mandatory before regulatory notification. Legal team reviewing liability exposure from historical false accusations.

auditLog.note: Raised following customer complaint regarding false fraud accusation

title: Missed Equipment Failure Prediction Causing Unplanned Downtime
description: The predictive maintenance AI model fails to identify developing equipment faults within the required prediction horizon, resulting in unexpected equipment failures, unplanned production downtime, safety incidents, and significant financial impact. Model performance has degraded due to distribution shift as equipment ages and operational conditions change.
comments: Model performance monitoring dashboard deployed. Retraining pipeline established with 6-monthly cadence. Hybrid human-AI review for high-criticality assets.

auditLog.note: Identified following unplanned downtime incident attributable to missed AI prediction

title: Industrial Sensor Data Transmitted to Overseas AI Vendor for Processing
description: Real-time industrial sensor data — which may contain operationally sensitive and potentially personal data — is continuously transmitted to an overseas AI vendor's cloud infrastructure for model inference and retraining. No NCA Cloud Cybersecurity Controls approval has been obtained, and the cross-border data transfer has not been assessed under PDPL Article 25.
comments: Data flow mapping completed. Legal and compliance review of transfer lawfulness initiated. Evaluating on-premise inference deployment as alternative to reduce cross-border transfer.

auditLog.note: Identified during NCA compliance review of AI vendor relationships

title: AI Maintenance Recommendations Not Interpretable by Engineering Staff
description: Maintenance engineers and operations staff cannot understand the basis of AI-generated maintenance recommendations, leading to blind trust in model outputs without appropriate critical evaluation. This prevents engineers from detecting erroneous recommendations and undermines the organisation's ability to demonstrate responsible human oversight to regulators.
comments: SHAP-based feature importance explanations added to maintenance dashboard. Engineer training on AI model interpretation completed for 80% of team. Remaining 20% scheduled for May.

auditLog.note: Raised during SDAIA transparency review of operational AI systems
SHAP explanations deployed. Engineer training initiated.
